profile_text.body:
Mila, also called the Quebec Artificial Intelligence Institute, is a nonprofit research institute based in Montreal, Quebec, Canada, founded in 1993. It describes itself as bringing together researchers from Université de Montréal, McGill University, Polytechnique Montréal and HEC Montréal, and as a community of more than 1,400 researchers specializing in machine learning. The institute says it is located in the heart of Quebec's AI ecosystem and frames its work around scientific excellence and innovation.

Its site presents research in several areas. One project proposes a generative cutout animation system that takes a skeletal animation and a text prompt and generates a 2.5D cutout rig for films and games, using an SDS loss with a LoRA prior. Another, QueStER, learns to generate keyword-based search specifications for generative retrieval, pairing a lightweight LLM with BM25 retrieval and training the rewriting policy with reinforcement learning. Mila also offers a course on using generative AI to support productivity at work, with the next cohort scheduled online for October 6 and 8, 2026, and it runs a venture arm that invests in founders working in deep tech, AI and STEM.

The material provided does not list any products, lawsuits or other legal matters for Mila.
